request: In each game's result, report the cause of death or the damage taken by source per minute, the number of action-model calls, and the goals completed or abandoned with reasons.
why: Without per-source damage and goal outcomes, games on the same seed can only be compared by survival time. That makes it hard to tell whether failures come from the build, the routing or the move choices.

why: Without names I cannot tell which evolutions a surviving build had, and evolutions seem to separate survivors from deaths.

status: partly done in 3e7ca4e: gyms are now built in 5-minute stages, each saved, and a death replays only that stage from its start, up to 3 times, so a 16:40 gym no longer needs one unbroken 17-minute life. A gym built at 15:00 plus a 300s game reaches 20:00, so the 300s cap stays. Gyms from the full run are declined: the full run plays the evaluation seed, and training on its states would tune the playbook to that one map, which the loop forbids. Also: a coach can now only retire its own gyms (the other coach retired one your games needed)
request: Let the loop save a gym from a full run (or from any game) at a chosen game time, for example a checkpoint at 16:40 of the evaluation-seed full run, and allow training games longer than 300s (e.g. 600s).
why: Building 15:00-17:00 gyms by replaying natural runs usually dies on the way, and the loop cannot test the 17:00 Compost Titan and 18:00 Ketchup Kraken, which killed both full runs, without a reliable late state.

status: done in dc813e0: knobs dashThreshold (default 0.5), and bossDashThreshold that replaces it while a boss is within bossDashRange (0 turns it off). Usable from loop 5.
request: Expose the action.dash threshold as a knob (dashThreshold, default 0.5), optionally with a separate lower threshold when a boss is within a given range.
why: In the L3.I10 full run the dash prompt scored 36-39% against the Mascot and never passed 0.5, so a charge was never saved for the 52-hp hit that killed the run. A threshold knob would let the loop test boss dashing without rewriting the prompt, which can only move the score indirectly.
